idiom_name: keyword arguments with defaults (def initialize(host:, port: 3000)) plus Data.define/Struct
implementation_notes: Ruby keyword arguments carry names and defaults at the call site (Client.new(host: "db", retries: 0)), and Data.define (3.2+) or Struct give record-like classes whose constructors accept keywords; Data members are mandatory, so an optional setting is expressed by overriding initialize with defaulted keywords and calling super. The classic builder survives for incremental, lazy construction - ActiveRecord::Relation accumulates where/order clauses and only runs the query when the relation is enumerated - and as a block DSL that evaluates instance_eval against a configuration object (RSpec, FactoryBot, Rails config blocks).
code_sketch:
Account = Data.define(:owner, :currency) do
  def initialize(owner:, currency: "EUR")   # default via keyword
    super
  end
end

a = Account.new(owner: "ada")               # => #<data Account owner="ada", currency="EUR">
b = Account.new(owner: "ada", currency: "USD")
pitfalls: Data members are all mandatory: making a field optional means overriding initialize and calling super with a filled-in default, and a mistake there turns the optional attribute back into a required keyword.
Keyword arguments are matched at runtime, so a typo raises ArgumentError only when that method runs, and a definition ending in **opts swallows unknown keys silently.
Block builders using instance_eval rebind self inside the block and hide the caller's own methods; use instance_exec with explicit arguments when the block needs outer context.
